items.title: Burrill Crohn interviewed by Monk Rowe, Woodstock, New York, January 3, 2012
items.q: Bruce Ricker... went on to become friends with Clint Eastwood.

ctx.x: Oh, yeah. Do you think people get the wrong idea, like oh you’re making a film, you’re going to make a lot of money on your film — I said a joke didn’t I?

Well yes and no. First of all, there are exceptions to every rule. And you know I’m crying poor here, but there was a period in my life when I did the “History of Jazz” series, there was a market for jazz films. And I had what they call a syndicator in England. He had a company called TCB, meaning taking care of business. His name was Angus Trowbridge — it’s a great British name — but he was an American and he lived outside of London. And he would go around to Cannes and different names of film festivals where…

knowledgeable. He’s just a good guy all around and he’s been very prolific. And he always finds money to make films. I don’t think he makes a lot of money when he makes them, but then the TV sales and — well you’d have to talk to him. I don’t know what his economic thing is.
